concerns.concern: The claimed performance advantage of the composite is not shown. The large gain in effective conductivity is roughly cancelled by an SSE coefficient about 10× smaller than in bilayers, and the power factor or power density is never compared with conventional devices.
concerns.quote: The ~10× loss in S thus roughly cancels the ~10²–10³ gain in σ_eff.

concerns.concern: There is no spin-Hall-angle control to confirm that the signal comes from inverse spin Hall detection. Composites should be made with a metal of negligible spin Hall angle (Cu, Au) and one of opposite sign (W, Ta).
concerns.quote: Sign reversal with W/Ta would be strong evidence for ISHE detection.

concerns.concern: There is no non-magnetic matrix control. Pt-coated non-magnetic garnet powders processed identically are needed to rule out Pt-intrinsic, processing-induced or field-dependent thermal artifacts.
concerns.quote: Pt-coated non-magnetic garnet powders (e.g., GGG or YAG) processed identically.

concerns.concern: The magnetization data appear to carry the wrong units. Values plotted as emu/g are about 1000× too small and are likely raw moment, which invalidates the argument that a lower saturation magnetization rules out a ferromagnetic-metal phase.
concerns.quote: The y-axis values are about three orders of magnitude too small for mass magnetization.

concerns.concern: XRD cannot exclude Fe₃O₄ at relevant levels. Its strongest reflection overlaps a YIG peak, and lab XRD detection limits are about 1–5 wt%, so XRD should not be the main basis for excluding ANE.
concerns.quote: The strongest Fe₃O₄ reflection, (311) at ~35.4° (Cu Kα), overlaps almost exactly with YIG (422) at ~35.5°.

concerns.concern: The α-Fe₂O₃ and YFeO₃ phases are also not excluded, since the authors admit they cannot be distinguished in the XRD. α-Fe₂O₃ is also weakly ferromagnetic at room temperature.
concerns.quote: could not be distinguished in the XRD data" means these phases are not excluded either.

concerns.concern: High-resolution STEM-EDS/EELS line profiles across Pt/YIG interfaces in the sintered samples, especially those pressed at 300 °C, are needed to check for Fe–Pt intermixing.
concerns.quote: high-resolution STEM-EDS/EELS line profiles across Pt/YIG interfaces in the *sintered* samples

concerns.concern: The field dependence of the signal should be overlaid on the normalized magnetization curve, measured in the same geometry with demagnetization accounted for, for both configurations.
concerns.quote: overlay normalized E(H) on normalized M(H), measured in the same geometry with demagnetization accounted for

concerns.concern: An uncoated-YIG pellet control is missing. Even a fragile pellet or YIG mixed with an inert binder would help.
concerns.quote: even a fragile pellet, or YIG mixed with an inert binder, would help.

concerns.concern: If the magnetization data are normalized, the roughly 25% reduction that does not depend on Pt thickness is too large to be Pt dilution. It suggests degraded YIG surfaces, which would affect the spin-mixing conductance. Pt mass fractions should be reported and the origin discussed.
concerns.quote: A thickness-independent ~25% drop instead suggests degraded YIG, such as magnetically dead or damaged surface layers

concerns.concern: A uniform decrease in magnetization cannot exclude a minor ferromagnetic-metal phase at about the 1 wt% level, because Pt dilution would mask it.
concerns.quote: A uniform decrease in M also cannot exclude a minor FMM phase at the ~1 wt% level

concerns.concern: The 37.9 emu/g comparison value is the near-0 K magnetization of YIG. The room-temperature value of about 27 emu/g should be used for 300 K data.
concerns.quote: 37.9 emu/g corresponds to YIG near 0 K. The room-temperature value is ~27 emu/g

concerns.concern: No physical or effective-medium model links bilayer parameters, grain size and Pt fraction to the composite SSE and power factor. Such a model is needed to judge whether 10–17 nV/K is plausible and to give design rules.
concerns.quote: The paper would be much stronger with even a simple effective-medium or circuit model

concerns.concern: A reference YIG-slab/Pt bilayer should be measured in the same setup with the same thermal-gradient determination. This would serve as calibration, as a fair comparison, and as a check of the signal's sign.
concerns.quote: ideally measure a reference YIG-slab/Pt bilayer in the same setup with the same ∇T determination

concerns.concern: The two measurement configurations use different thermal setups with unquantified interfacial resistances, so the close agreement of the two S values may be fortuitous. The thermal gradient should be measured on the sample itself and an uncertainty budget given.
concerns.quote: The 14.8 vs 14.4 nV/K agreement may be partly fortuitous.

concerns.concern: The pressing axis, sample dimensions and electrode spacing are not given. Uniaxial pressing may make conductivity and thermal conductivity anisotropic, so conductivity should be measured along the voltage direction used in each configuration.
concerns.quote: The pressing axis relative to x, y and z, and the sample dimensions and electrode spacing, are not given.

concerns.concern: Contrasting the composite's isotropy with a rotated thin film is not very informative, because the composite is isotropic by construction apart from pressing-induced texture.
concerns.quote: Contrasting it with a rotated thin film is therefore not very informative.

concerns.concern: Only one sample per condition from a single batch is reported. Replicate samples and uncertainties for σ_eff, κ and S are needed before the trends can be treated as physical.
concerns.quote: Only one sample per condition is reported, all from a single batch.

concerns.concern: The observed trends are not explained, including why 300 °C pressing roughly halves S compared with room-temperature pressing and why σ_eff grows superlinearly with Pt thickness. Possible interfacial changes should be discussed.
concerns.quote: The trends are presented as physically meaningful but are not explained or tested for reproducibility

concerns.concern: The Pt thickness dependence is called consistent with bilayer behavior, but bilayer shunting would predict about a factor of 2 between 15 and 30 nm, whereas about 1.2 is observed.
concerns.quote: bilayer shunting for t ≫ λ_s would predict roughly a factor of 2 between 15 and 30 nm, against the observed ~1.2.

concerns.concern: The 15 and 30 nm Pt thicknesses are nominal values inferred from deposition time and should be verified by TEM or mass gain.
concerns.quote: They should be verified by TEM or by mass gain.

concerns.concern: The "2–3 orders of magnitude" conductivity improvement is overstated. The lowest composite value is only about 10× the best literature value, so the range is about 1–3 orders.
concerns.quote: Even setting PF aside, the "2–3 orders of magnitude" figure is generous.

concerns.concern: Literature σ_eff values depend on the arbitrarily chosen substrate or slab thickness, which weakens σ_eff as a figure of merit.
concerns.quote: A thinner YIG slab raises σ_eff without any architectural change, which weakens σ_eff as a figure of merit.

concerns.concern: zT should be reported (about 8×10⁻¹¹ from the authors' own numbers) so readers can judge the claim of a scalable bulk thermoelectric platform.
concerns.quote: report zT. From the authors' own numbers, zT = PF·T/κ ≈ 5×10⁻¹³ × 300 / 1.87 ≈ 8×10⁻¹¹.

concerns.concern: Attributing the low thermal conductivity to interfacial phonon scattering is unsupported. Porosity and inter-particle contact resistance likely dominate, and an uncoated reference or effective-medium estimate is needed.
concerns.quote: Attributing the low κ to "phonon scattering at the YIG/Pt interface" is not supported

concerns.concern: Relative densities are computed against YIG alone. Including the Pt mass would raise the theoretical density and lower the reported relative densities.
concerns.quote: The relative densities are computed against YIG alone (5.11 g/cm³).

concerns.concern: The particle size distribution of the crushed YIG is not reported, although it matters for the expected grain-size dependence of the SSE relative to the magnon length.
concerns.quote: Both effects depend on the particle size distribution, which is not reported

concerns.concern: The Pt EDS map suggests Pt is concentrated in fine-particle regions, with large Pt-free areas over large grains. The homogeneity of the Pt network should be addressed.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2c: the Pt EDS map appears concentrated in regions of fine particles, with large Pt-free areas over large grains.

concerns.concern: Interface quality is not controlled or characterized: there is no surface cleaning before sputtering, pressing is done in air, and there is only one TEM image of the 5 nm sample. TEM of the 15/30 nm sintered samples is requested.
concerns.quote: Interfacial quality, the main determinant of g↑↓, is not characterized beyond one TEM image of the 5 nm sample.

concerns.concern: The statement that Pt thicknesses well above the spin diffusion length ensure clear SSE observation conflates film continuity with thickness. A thickness much greater than λ_s actually reduces the ISHE field through shunting.
concerns.quote: conflates two issues. Continuity is a growth question; t ≫ λ_s actually reduces E_ISHE through shunting.

concerns.concern: The term "bad metal regime" is inappropriate for a percolating composite, and comparisons with undoped Si/Ge are not meaningful. Practical thermoelectrics or transverse thermoelectric bulk materials would be better comparisons.
concerns.quote: "Bad metal regime" has a specific meaning tied to the Mott–Ioffe–Regel limit in intrinsic conductors and is inappropriate for a percolating composite.

concerns.concern: Prior art on scalable SSE (spin-Seebeck coatings, FM-oxide/metal multilayers) should be cited, and the novelty relative to Boona et al. stated more precisely.
concerns.quote: the context of scalable SSE should cite spin-Seebeck coatings (Kirihara et al., Nat. Mater. 2012) and FM-oxide/metal multilayers

concerns.concern: The paragraph on α-Fe₂O₃/YFeO₃ is logically awkward and grammatically incomplete.
concerns.quote: logically awkward ("could not be distinguished … suggest that they are inert") and grammatically incomplete

concerns.concern: Field symmetrization is mislabeled: it should be antisymmetrization to remove field-even components, both for the SSE data and for the Hall data in Methods.
concerns.quote: "symmetrized with respect to H to remove field-even components" should read *antisymmetrized*.

concerns.concern: On p. 7 a measurement configuration is mislabeled; H_x–∇_zT should read H_z–∇_xT.
concerns.quote: "consistent with that obtained in the H_x–∇_zT configuration (Figs. 3c and S5)" should read H_z–∇_xT.

concerns.concern: SI Note S2 cites the wrong figure (Fig. S2) for the XRD data; it should be Fig. S3.
concerns.quote: SI Note S2 repeatedly refers to "Fig. S2" for XRD; it should be Fig. S3.

concerns.concern: The Cu Kα wavelength is given inconsistently in Methods and SI.
concerns.quote: The Cu Kα wavelength is given as 0.15406 nm in Methods and 0.15418 nm in SI.

concerns.concern: Fig. S3 assigns the same diffraction card number to two different phases, Y₂O₃ and FePt.
concerns.quote: Fig. S3 assigns the same card number (PDF#43-0661) to both Y₂O₃ and FePt.

concerns.concern: The magnetometry instrument is inconsistent: Methods say SQUID, while the author contributions mention VSM.
concerns.quote: Methods state SQUID (MPMS); the author contributions mention VSM.

concerns.concern: The "This work" rows in Table S1 should be labeled by sample.
concerns.quote: Table S1: the "This work" rows should be labeled by sample

concerns.concern: The Fig. S4 caption omits that dashed reference lines also appear in panels (d) and (e).
concerns.quote: Fig. S4 caption: dashed reference lines also appear in panels (d) and (e), not only (b)–(c).

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3 caption sentence mapping the subscripts x, y, z to ∇T, I and H is confusing and should be rephrased.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3 caption: the sentence on subscripts x, y, z mapping to ∇T, I and H is confusing; please rephrase.

concerns.concern: There are typos and misspelled names, and the author name order should be checked.
concerns.quote: "It is worth nothing" → "noting"; "Galosov" → "Golosov"; check the author name order ("Hirata Keisuke").

concerns.concern: The "630% higher" power factor would be clearer stated as about 7× higher.
concerns.quote: The "630% higher" PF should be stated as "~7× higher", which is clearer.
